# edgeos_system_syslog (Resource)

Local logging to `/var/log/messages` (`system syslog global`). There is one per router; the resource takes over the existing settings.

Remote syslog servers are separate resources (`edgeos_system_syslog_host`), and so are extra log files (`edgeos_system_syslog_file`), the same way `edgeos_firewall_rule` is separate from `edgeos_firewall_name`. This resource never touches them, nor the `console` and `user` targets.

Only the attributes you set are managed. Removing an attribute from the configuration removes that setting from the router. Import reads every attribute.

Destroying the resource deletes the settings it manages. Without any global facility the router no longer writes `/var/log/messages`, so keep the resource with the EdgeOS defaults rather than destroying it if you want to stop managing it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The EdgeOS defaults, plus a larger archive.
resource "edgeos_system_syslog" "this" {
  facilities = {
    all       = "notice"
    protocols = "debug"
  }
  archive_files = 5
  archive_size  = 1024
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `archive_files` (Number) Number of rotated /var/log/messages files to keep (`archive files`). Unset leaves it alone.
- `archive_size` (Number) Size in kilobytes at which the /var/log/messages file is rotated (`archive size`). Unset leaves it alone.
- `facilities` (Map of String) Facilities to log and the lowest level logged for each (`facility <name> level <level>`), such as `{ all = "notice", protocols = "debug" }`. Facilities: `all`, `auth`, `authpriv`, `cron`, `daemon`, `kern`, `lpr`, `mail`, `mark`, `news`, `protocols`, `security`, `syslog`, `user`, `uucp`, `local0`, `local1`, `local2`, `local3`, `local4`, `local5`, `local6`, `local7`. Levels: `emerg`, `alert`, `crit`, `err`, `warning`, `notice`, `info`, `debug`. The resource owns the whole list: facilities that are not in the map are removed. EdgeOS ships with `{ all = "notice", protocols = "debug" }`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `syslog`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_system_syslog.this
  id = "syslog"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_system_syslog.this 'syslog'
```
